chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The fingers of the two hands and the two feet are equal in blood money (diyah); for each finger, ten camels, and for the nail, five dinars.

key_terms.إِبِل: Camels (traditional unit of currency/wealth in Islamic law)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or financial compensation for bodily injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money compensation for cutting a finger or toe in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the principle of equality among all digits in financial compensation (diyah), assigning ten camels per finger or toe and five dinars for the nail. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus on the uniformity of bodily parts in diya calculations, distinguishing it from other schools that may differentiate between fingers and toes based on specific textual interpretations.
